pages: Design reliable contracts for JavaScript programs

Signal Harbor routes cargo through a network of manifests, message queues, and partner docks. You are rebuilding the dispatch desk. Each level introduces one way to keep a program's promises visible as data moves between people, functions, and systems.

Begin with the Dockhand path if you are new to TypeScript. Work through the code in order. For each listing, predict a result, change one input, and check whether the compiler and the running program behave as you expected. The lessons use familiar JavaScript expressions and build up their type contracts gradually.

The Contract Engineer path develops APIs that express relationships between values. The Boundary Operator path emphasizes validation, failure, and integration. Check each standalone listing with tsc --strict --target ES2022 --noEmit. Node.js can run these listings by stripping the types, so run the compiler separately to check them. Validate external data at runtime.

Start with the beginner route if these ideas are new to you. In the game, choose a hero to save your checkpoint answers, code drafts, and quest log. The attached field kit contains the worked examples, starter files, and a quest journal.

Use inference for local values and annotations for the inputs and outputs of a small function.

TypeScript checks JavaScript programs before they run. Start with three common kinds of values: numbers for arithmetic, strings for text, and booleans for decisions. A declaration such as let load = 3 lets the checker infer number, so later assigning a string to load produces an error. const prevents reassignment and can preserve the exact literal type for a primitive value.
A function annotation describes the contract callers should follow. mass:
number gives the function a numeric input, and : string after the
parameter list commits it to returning text. Try returning mass directly. The return annotation catches the mistake inside the function, where the change is easiest to understand.

JavaScript still allows a number to be NaN, infinite, or negative. A type can establish that arithmetic is available, while a runtime condition establishes a domain rule. The example checks both inputs before multiplying and rejects an infinite result, which can occur even when both inputs are finite.
Remember. Type annotations describe permitted kinds of values. Runtime checks enforce business rules within those kinds.
Which value is allowed by the annotation count: number but should fail this cargo rule?

Implement palletLabel. A pallet carries ten crates. Return the number of pallets needed for a nonnegative safe integer crate count. Use the exact format Pallets: 2 for 11 crates and throw RangeError for an invalid count.

Checkpoint. C. The value 2.5 has type number, but the count must be an integer. The function needs the integer check even in a type-checked program.
Math.ceil(crateCount / 10) gives the number of pallets. Check the empty

A guard rejects negative, fractional, and non-finite counts. Division followed by rounding up handles exact multiples and partial pallets with one expression. Check 0, 10, and 11 crates to catch boundary errors.
Replace the fixed capacity with a parameter. Decide which capacities are valid and test an invalid capacity before checking the result.
Describe a record and let a function read a collection without granting it permission to mutate the input.

A cargo record has named fields. A type alias gives that shape a reusable name. Functions can state which fields they need, and TypeScript checks whether the supplied value has those fields with compatible types. An object held in a variable may carry extra fields and still be passed to a function expecting the smaller shape.
readonly Cargo[] makes the array read-only through that parameter. The

function can iterate and inspect its entries. It cannot push, sort in place, or assign a replacement element through that reference. Put readonly on the record fields as well if the function should be prevented from assigning through them.

Read-only types apply to the reference the checker sees. JavaScript may still hold another alias with write access. If a report must remain stable after the caller edits its own objects, construct a snapshot of the required data and decide how deeply it must be copied.
Remember. Describe the fields a caller must supply and the write access a callee should receive.
What does readonly Cargo[] prevent inside totalWeight?
A. Passing an array with extra fields on its records
B. Changing the array through the parameter
C. Another alias changing the original array
D. A weight being negative at runtime
Return the IDs of all cargo weighing at least 10 kg, in the same order as the input. Create a new array and leave the manifest alone.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. B. The read-only parameter restricts writes through that parameter. Record field mutability and other aliases have their own rules.
Try a loop that creates a fresh string[] before inspecting the first record.
Add the ID when weightKg >= 10. Test a record weighing exactly 10 kg.
Each selected ID is copied into a new array. The caller can add IDs to that output without changing the input array, and filtering preserves relative order.
Design a grouped report whose results can be read but cannot be edited through the type returned to a consumer.
Narrow a union by checking a literal tag before reading fields that belong to one case.

An arrival either has a dock assignment or is waiting for a reason. Model both shapes with a union. Each shape carries a kind field with a different literal value. The compiler can follow a comparison with that field and make the corresponding shape available inside the branch.

A single object type with optional dock and reason fields would permit a waiting arrival with no reason. A tagged union makes the appropriate fields required for each case. A structurally compatible value can still carry extra properties. Check the tag before using the fields required for that branch.
When testing an optional primitive, check for the missing state you mean.
if (dock) treats zero as false, even if dock zero is a valid location. dock !== undefined makes the distinction explicit. For a tagged union, checking kind
avoids mixing a status decision with the truthiness of a field.
Remember. A discriminant lets the compiler track which fields exist after a runtime check.
Which property can you access after arrival.kind === 'waiting' succeeds?
Implement canUnload. An assigned arrival can unload only if its dock is open. A waiting arrival cannot unload. Use the dock list as read-only input.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. A. The literal tag narrows the union to the waiting case, where reason is required.
Narrow the union using arrival.kind before you access arrival.dock.
Use openDocks.includes(arrival.dock) inside the assigned branch, or combine both conditions with &&.
The status test establishes which shape is present. The membership test establishes whether that dock is open. Both decisions matter, including when the assignment is to dock zero.
Add a diverted case carrying a destination harbor. Give it a distinct message in statusText.
Pass a typed function as an argument and preserve meaningful falsy values when applying a default.
Two dock reports can traverse the same manifest while counting different things. Pass a rule as a function. A parameter of type (cargo: Cargo) =>
boolean promises that the report supplies a cargo record and expects the
rule to say whether it belongs in the count.

An arrow function written directly at the call site usually inherits its parameter type from the expected callback type. The checker can suggest valid fields even if the arrow parameter has no annotation. Read the parameter type and the return type together when deciding whether a callback is suitable.
?? applies its right-hand value only when the left side is null or undefined.
The example accepts an optional maximum, validates any supplied maximum as a nonnegative safe integer, and defaults to no limit. A maximum of zero means select nothing. ?? preserves that value.
Remember. Give reusable traversal a callback contract and make the default policy explicit.
Why does the example use maximum ?? Infinity?
B. It converts strings to numbers
C. It throws when the argument is absent
D. It preserves an explicit zero maximum
Implement labelMatching. Call label once per weight that passes weight >= 0 and return the labels in input order. Negative weights and NaN fail this test.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. D. Zero is distinct from undefined, so ?? keeps the zero and
Build a fresh array. Use the positive test weight >= 0 to decide whether to append a label.
Call label(weight) once per retained item. Zero is nonnegative and should reach the callback.

The traversal owns the decision to include an item. The callback owns the presentation. A callback that records its inputs can show whether the traversal invokes it for the correct items and in the right order.
Add a test callback that throws on its second call. Explain what the caller observes and whether the partial result ever escapes.
Turn untrusted JSON into a checked record by combining unknown with small runtime checks.

A partner can send malformed JSON or valid JSON with the wrong shape. A TypeScript interface describes the shape your program expects. Annotating a value with that interface cannot verify bytes received from a file or the network. Give parsed input the type unknown so the checker requires evidence before you use its fields.

A JSON parse may throw before a value exists. After parsing, require a non-null, non-array object. The in checks let TypeScript read the named fields as unknown. Object.hasOwn requires the fields on the record itself. Then check value types and domain rules such as a nonempty trimmed ID or a finite, nonnegative weight.

Construct a new record from the fields you validated. That tells readers which values crossed the boundary, and gives your internal type a clean starting point. An as Manifest assertion would change what the checker believes while leaving a malformed value untouched.
Remember. Let runtime evidence earn the internal type at every untrusted boundary.
What does JSON.parse(raw) as Manifest verify at runtime?
A. That the parsed object has an id
B. That each field has its declared type
D. That a weight is nonnegative
Decode a dock status from raw JSON. Require a non-array record with its own nonnegative safe integer dock and boolean open. Return undefined for a syntax or shape error.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. C. JSON.parse checks syntax and may throw. The assertion is erased during compilation, so it does not inspect the result's shape.
Assign JSON.parse to an unknown variable inside a try block. Handle null before checking properties.
Narrow both fields with in and require own properties with Object.hasOwn. Check open with typeof so false is accepted.

A valid object with dock: 0 and open: false should pass. The strings "0" and "false" should fail. Testing those pairs proves the implementation checks types instead of relying on truthiness or coercion.
Return an error code that distinguishes invalid JSON from a missing field and a field with the wrong type.
Await a promise, handle rejection, and keep a real value distinct from a failed request.

An asynchronous operation can produce a value later. Promise<number> describes the value on fulfillment. Inside an async function, await obtains that value or throws when the promise rejects. The surrounding function still returns a promise, so its caller needs to await it or otherwise observe its outcome.

Place the await inside try when you want that function to translate a rejection. If the operation resolves to zero, zero is data. A separate error case lets the caller tell whether the harbor is quiet or the status report could not be fetched.
Rejected promises can carry arbitrary values. An error created with new
Error has a message. A thrown string or plain object requires a separate
policy. The example keeps its public failure message stable, while a real service might log a narrowed error privately for diagnosis.
Remember. Await where you can act on rejection and use a distinct state for failure.
If the loader resolves with 0, which result should reportTide fulfill with?
A. { ok: false, message: 'Tide report unavailable' }
Implement readGate. Await the injected status function, return open or closed on success, and return offline if the function throws or rejects.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. B. A fulfilled promise can carry zero. The catch branch applies to a thrown error or rejected promise, regardless of the fulfillment values.
Await the callback inside the try block so synchronous throws and rejections share the same failure branch.
Map a resolved false to closed. Use offline only inside catch.
A gate may be reachable and closed. Treating false as a request failure would conflate operational state with connectivity. Test resolved true, resolved false, and rejection.
Preserve a safe diagnostic string on the offline result without assuming every rejected value is an Error.
Assemble validation and routing into a small public module with a clear interface.

A module can keep local helpers private and export the pieces other code should use. In this dispatch module the caller sees the decision contract and one routing function. The normalization step stays private because the caller does not need to depend on the exact trimming and uppercasing procedure.

A regular import can name a value the JavaScript runtime needs, such as a function. import type names a TypeScript declaration used only during checking and disappears from the emitted JavaScript. When you split the example into files, use the module settings and file specifiers required by your runtime. In a Node ESM setup that runs emitted JavaScript, a relative import of the compiled module can use ./dispatch.js in the TypeScript source.

Keep routing separate from input and output. A pure decision function lets tests pass it a destination without opening a terminal or contacting a dock. A separate adapter can read the input, invoke the function, and show the result. Keep the exported return type explicit so a refactor cannot quietly change the public outcomes.
Remember. Export the contract a caller needs and test the decision logic independently of its input adapter.
Which declaration should a caller use when it only needs the Decision type for checking?
Implement a module function that routes north to dock 1 and south to dock 2 after normalizing case and whitespace. Report invalid for other values. Export the decision type and the function.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. A. import type gives the checker access to the declaration and emits no runtime import for it.
Normalize once using trim() and toUpperCase().
Test north, SOUTH , and a destination with no matching branch.

A caller can switch on the tagged decision without parsing a message or catching an exception for an ordinary invalid destination. The standalone module can be tested with simple inputs and no infrastructure.
Build a separate presentation module that imports the type and formats each decision. Keep text formatting out of the routing module.
Use a generic key constraint and indexed access to preserve the relationship between a property name and its value.

A helper that reads one property should return the type of that specific property. keyof T names the keys of the object type, while T[K] is the type of a property at key K. A generic parameter K extends keyof T ties a caller's key to the object, so a typo fails checking and a precise key preserves a precise result.

Compare two different outputs when reading a string ID and a number capacity. A return type written as T[keyof T] would allow any property value type, so both calls would return a union. Capturing the selected key as its own parameter retains information already present at the call site.

An externally supplied string still needs a runtime decision about which fields are permitted. When the key is a union of known keys, its value type is a corresponding union. The generic relationship expresses exactly what was known at the call site and cannot make an unknown key safe by itself.
Remember. Capture the caller's selected key as a type parameter when the result depends on that key.
What type should field(dock, 'capacity') infer for the shown dock object?
Implement a helper that gets a property from each object in a read-only list. Keep the output type linked to the selected property, so choosing a numeric field gives number[].
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. D. The literal key capacity determines K. Indexing the inferred dock type with that key gives number.
The key constraint establishes that row[key] can be read for every row of type T.
Return rows.map(row => row[key]) and assign the result to a variable typed as the expected property array.
The same code can return string[] or number[] because the return type keeps the key relationship. Test an empty list and a list of several objects with both key kinds.
Accept an allowlisted field name from a text input and explain where the runtime narrowing occurs before calling pluck.
Derive related record shapes and use satisfies to check configuration without assigning a wider type to it.

An operations record and its editable patch often share fields. A mapped type can copy each allowed field while applying a modifier. The example excludes id, which remains stable, and makes every remaining field optional. A new field in the original record automatically becomes available to the patch according to this policy.
An absent patch property means leave the value alone. This example's runtime also preserves the previous value for explicit undefined. Enable
exactOptionalPropertyTypes separately from strict if callers should be
required to omit an optional property whose declared value type excludes
undefined. Check untrusted patch values at the boundary.

Use satisfies when an expression needs to conform to a shape and you also want to work with the expression's own inferred type. The registry example checks that each required dock has a valid entry. as const preserves the literal capacity values and gives a read-only view in the type system. Neither construct freezes the runtime object.
Remember. Derive shape changes from the source contract and spell out what omission means.
What does the satisfies Record<...> check on defaultDocks?
A. The registry has the required keys and compatible capacity values
B. The object is frozen when JavaScript runs
C. Every capacity is a positive integer
D. All later reads return the same capacity after mutation
Define a patch type derived from Dock that allows changes to capacity and open only. Apply an omitted patch field by preserving the previous value. Preserve false and zero when explicitly provided.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. A. The checker validates the expression against the required shape. The literal types come from as const, and runtime values still follow JavaScript rules.
Partial<Omit<Dock, 'id'>> expresses the same shape as the mapped type
Read only the fields you intend to update. Use ?? so false and zero survive.

A type-level patch narrows the API for typed callers. Reading the specific editable fields at runtime also protects the identifier if an object with extra properties reaches this function through structural compatibility.
Add a removable note and decide how to represent preserve, replace, and clear as three different operations.
Build a finite state transition and make a missing case fail TypeScript checking with never.

Operations gain states as they move through the harbor. A queued job can start, a running job can complete, and a completed job stays completed. Store the tag and any state-specific fields together so a job can never be both completed and waiting in the typed state model.

A switch can narrow the state across every branch. At the end, a function accepting never makes the expectation of complete coverage visible to the checker. Add a fourth state and the old switch will produce a type error at the call to that function until the new case is handled.

Exhaustive handling checks the listed variants. Whether a transition is legal depends on the domain. Keep the transition pure while you are designing it, then let a caller decide when to persist the new state or perform an effect. Validate input at the boundary before the transition receives it.
Remember. Pair a tagged state model with an exhaustive switch and explicit transition rules.
What happens if Job gains a cancelled variant and advance stays as written?
A. Cancelled automatically falls into completed
B. The never check fails because cancelled remains unhandled
C. The compiler silently adds a cancelled branch
D. Queued jobs can no longer be constructed
Add a cancelled state with a reason. Update advance so cancelled and completed jobs are terminal, queued jobs become running, and running jobs complete. Keep the exhaustive check.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. B. A cancelled job would reach the default branch, so the argument could not be assigned to the parameter typed as never.
Extend the union with { state: 'cancelled'; id: string; reason: string
Return the same job object in terminal branches so the cancellation reason is retained.
Each state has a clear successor. The compiler checks that every declared variant is handled, while tests can assert that terminal states keep their original data.
Represent a retry event and return a typed rejection if someone tries to retry a completed job.
Keep a message's tag correlated with the payload expected by its handler.

The message board carries different payloads for arrivals and departures. Keep the payload attached to its literal tag in one discriminated object. A handler switch then narrows the pair together. If you split the tag and payload into two independent union-typed variables, a caller could pair the wrong payload with a valid tag.

A payload map gives every event name a contract. A mapped type can derive one tagged object per key, and indexing the resulting object type with the whole key union produces a union of those cases. The example uses this to keep the event declaration in one place.

The dispatcher still needs a branch for each event it handles. A table of callbacks can also express event-specific parameter types, but calling a handler selected by a union key needs evidence that its argument corresponds to that key. Keep the association explicit at the call site and use an exhaustive switch when it is the clearest way to show the correlation.
Remember. Construct a union of valid tag and payload pairs and preserve the pair through dispatch.
What is the benefit of deriving Notice as a union from Payloads?
A. It automatically validates external JSON messages
B. It guarantees the runtime delivery order
C. It ties each literal event tag to that event's own payload
D. It makes every payload optional
Add a delay notice with a vessel and a number of minutes. Produce Gull
delayed 5 min for that case and keep the switch exhaustive.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. C. The mapped type builds each allowed pairing separately. The union does not admit a depart tag with an arrive payload.
Add the event and payload in the map. The Notice union will pick up the new key automatically.
Add a delay branch and read both fields from notice.payload after narrowing the tag.
The type map is the source of the payload contract. The switch ties the runtime behavior to that contract, and its default never assignment detects a forgotten branch when a message type is added.
Define a handler-table type from Payloads that requires one correctly typed callback for each event name.
Represent the outcome of each asynchronous request while keeping the relationship to the original input order.

The scheduler can ask several docks for a status independently. Starting each request before awaiting them allows overlap. A sequential loop with an await before launching the next request is appropriate when an operation depends on the previous result or when the service requires serial access.
Promise.all returns fulfillment values in input order if every input fulfills.
It rejects if any input rejects, and the remaining work may still continue.
Promise.allSettled lets you inspect every outcome. Another approach is to
catch rejection inside each operation, convert it to an explicit failure result, and gather those fulfilled result objects with Promise.all.

The example preserves the dock identifier in each result. That makes a failure actionable after results are filtered or logged separately. This example starts one operation for every input. A production scheduler with an unbounded list should add an explicit limit on active requests and decide whether it supports cancellation.
Remember. Choose a collection operation whose error behavior matches what the caller needs to retain.
If the second dock answers before the first and both finish, which order does probeAll return?
D. The same order as docks
Implement probeAll using an injected query. Preserve the order and name of every dock, returning a failure result for just the docks whose queries throw or reject.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. D. Promise.all preserves input order in its output array, even when individual operations finish in a different order.
Use an async helper or typed async map callback so each operation catches its own failure.
Pass the resulting promises to Promise.all. Return a Probe in both branches of the per-dock operation.

A failed request no longer discards successes from other docks. A result carries its identity, and the ordered array can still be paired with the caller's inputs. Verify a mix of true, false, and a rejection.
Sketch how you would enforce at most four active queries. Identify where an active slot is released on failure.
Validate a string once at the boundary and give the checked identifier a distinct compile-time type.

Dock IDs and shipment IDs may both be strings. A function accepting either as a plain string cannot catch callers that mix up the two. A brand creates a type-level distinction using an intersection with a unique marker. A checked constructor is then the normal route from an untrusted string to the stronger type.

The parser in this example checks the entire identifier before asserting the brand. The assertion is small and sits directly after the runtime evidence. At runtime the value remains a string. Serializing it sends the text, and a receiving service should validate that text against its own boundary contract.

A format check says that an ID looks valid. It cannot prove that a corresponding shipment exists, belongs to a caller, or can be modified. Perform those checks in the service that owns the records. A useful brand name reflects the specific guarantee the parser establishes.
Remember. Keep the brand assertion beside the runtime check that establishes its limited guarantee.
What guarantee does a value from parseShipmentId carry?
A. Its format is S- followed by four ASCII digits
C. The current caller owns the shipment
D. The JavaScript value carries a runtime symbol property
Make a distinct DockId brand and a parser that accepts D- followed by exactly two ASCII digits. The value should be usable as a string after checking.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. A. The regular expression validates the format. The brand is compile-time information, and database existence and authorization require separate evidence.
Start by checking typeof value === 'string' and then match
Return the branded assertion only after a successful match. Test D-00,
The format check accepts zero digits inside an otherwise valid ID and rejects a shipment prefix. The separate marker lets functions enforce which category of checked ID they expect.
Add a lookup that can return missing for a valid-looking dock ID. Explain why that check belongs after parsing.
Connect a runtime decoder to a typed decision and a small duplicate guard with an explicit boundary.

A transport delivers the same dispatch instruction twice. A command ID gives the dispatch desk a way to recognize a repeat. Start by validating a parsed value before creating a command. Give the command a literal destination union so the rest of the application works with a short list of valid destinations.

A Map can remember which destination an ID was assigned to. A repeated command with the same destination gets a duplicate response, and reusing an ID for another destination gets a conflict. The policy matters because treating a different command as a harmless repeat could hide an upstream bug. Return tagged decisions so callers can report each case distinctly.

This example makes a decision and records it synchronously in a single in-memory map. Its duplicate guarantee ends when that map is discarded. A real service needs durable state, a defined retention period, and a plan to coordinate deduplication with the side effect. Do not infer exactly-once delivery from a type annotation or the presence of an ID.
Remember. Validate at the boundary, keep decisions explicit, and state the lifetime of every operational guarantee.
What should dispatch return if an ID used for north arrives again with destination south?
A. Route it to dock 2 as a new ID
D. Treat it as an identical duplicate

Implement handle with a supplied Map. A command is a non-array record with its own nonblank string id and to of 'north' or 'south'. Trim the id. Return invalid for malformed commands, route for a fresh ID, duplicate for a matching repeat, and conflict if a repeat changes the destination. Only a fresh route updates the map.
Read the debrief   ·   Back to the field manual
Checkpoint. B. The same ID now refers to different work. Reporting a conflict preserves the first decision and makes the mismatched repeat visible.
Narrow the input before looking it up. Extract the trimmed ID and destination only after checking both.
Compare a saved destination with the incoming destination. Add the ID only on the fresh route path.

Test one valid route, an identical repeat, a repeat for another destination, and an invalid object. Check the map after each call. These cases distinguish validation, conflict detection, and the one path that changes state.
Sketch a restart-safe version. Define what is persisted, how long command IDs are retained, and what outcome a caller should see if delivery fails after dispatch recorded the ID.
